html_en:
The AI industry delivered a day of seismic shifts, from Andrej Karpathy's surprising move to Anthropic to Google's aggressive push into agentic AI, while enterprise leaders grapple with the new economics of AI deployment.

The Great Migration: Karpathy Joins Anthropic

The day's biggest surprise came from Andrej Karpathy, who announced his move to Anthropic after departing OpenAI earlier this year.
"Personal update: I've joined Anthropic. I think the next few years at the frontier of LLMs will be especially formative. I am very excited to join the team here and get back to R&D. I remain deeply passionate about education and plan to resume my work on it in time."
The announcement garnered massive attention with over 130,000 likes, signaling the industry's recognition of Karpathy's influence. His move reflects the continuing talent wars at the frontier of AI research, with Dan Shipper capturing the broader sentiment: "what did karpathy see" Matt Turck couldn't resist the moment, joking that "Anthropic attains sainthood, officially annointed by AI Jesus", while Tom Rubin at Anthropic simply declared: "the future is bright, lets get to work".

Google's Agent Offensive

Google made aggressive moves across multiple fronts, signaling their renewed focus on agentic AI. The company launched Gemini Spark, their "24/7 personal AI agent designed to proactively manage tasks," rolling out to trusted testers this week and Google AI Ultra subscribers next week. More significantly, Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash, showing substantial performance improvements. Aaron Levie at Box shared impressive evaluation results:
"Gemini 3.5 Flash is out, and it's a major jump over Gemini 3 Flash in model capability for knowledge work... the model delivers a 12 percentage point jump on complex document tasks."
Levie's detailed breakdown showed dramatic improvements across industries: financial services (+8pp), public sector (+17pp), healthcare (+22pp), and life sciences (+20pp). Matt Turck noted Google's momentum: "Genuinely impressive release by Google today (remember when they were behind?)" highlighting the 76.2% score on Terminal-Bench for agentic coding and 56.5% on Toolathon for real-world tasks. Google also expanded Project Genie with Street View grounding, allowing users to "generate worlds starting from real places" and introduced their Computational Discovery platform powered by AlphaEvolve.

The New Economics of AI: Token Wars and Capacity Constraints

Enterprise AI spending emerged as a critical pain point. Aaron Levie reported from a dinner with Fortune 500 CIOs:
"Token costs will become a dominant topic in enterprises going forward with AI... this was the most heated topic. A mix of strategies are being employed, but basically no one feels like they have the right solution."
The discussion revealed companies struggling with prioritizing workloads, setting spend caps by team, and justifying AI use cases—all while underlying costs constantly evolve. Meanwhile, Sam Altman announced OpenAI's response: offering discounted tokens for 1-3 year commitments as "customers are increasingly asking us for certainty on capacity." The company also offered $2M in tokens to every Y Combinator startup, betting on the rise of "tokenmaxxing" companies.

Enterprise AI Infrastructure Evolves

Anthropic made significant infrastructure announcements with their Managed Agents platform, introducing self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels. The move addresses enterprise security concerns by allowing companies to keep sensitive data within their own perimeters while leveraging Anthropic's orchestration.
"The sandbox runs on your own infrastructure, or with managed providers like Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, or Vercel to handle the compute and isolation for you."
Guillermo Rauch at Vercel highlighted the integration, showing how "Claude Managed Agents 🤝 Vercel Sandbox" enables secure agent execution. The podcast episode with Serval's Jake Stauch provided deeper insight into this infrastructure evolution. Stauch explained how AI-native enterprise service management differs from traditional ServiceNow approaches:
"We took this unique approach of let's keep those primitives, workflows on top of databases, but allow you to use AI to build the workflows and use AI to update the databases."
Watch/Listen: Rebuilding IT From the Ground Up for the AI Age: Serval's Jake Stauch

Developer Velocity in the AI Era

The development workflow continues rapid transformation. Ryan Lou shared his current stack: "i now use: Composer 2.5 for planning, Composer 2.5 for building & iterations, Composer 2.5 for debugging", highlighting AI's role as an "all-rounder, especially for UI work." swyx outlined his comprehensive "AI SDLC" process, emphasizing the importance of comprehensive testing, refactoring for AI editing, and autonomous execution. His approach reflects the broader industry shift toward AI-first development practices. Nikunj Arora captured the broader implications: "we have already gone from assistant -> coworker -> and soon entering autonomous workers", noting that while true autonomy doesn't work yet, "the harnesses and the model capabilities are going to get us there within this area for a large faction of jobs." The industry appears to be entering what Arora calls "the diffusion era" where AI becomes embedded in everything we do—a process that will take "the next 10-20 years or as I call it the last mile of the last mile."
html_zh:
AI基础设施正在经历一次重大转变。从Andrej Karpathy加入Anthropic的震撼消息，到Google发布强大的Gemini 3.5 Flash，再到企业对AI代理的需求激增，今天的AI生态系统正在快速成熟并走向产业化。

🌟 人才流动重塑AI格局

今天AI界最重磅的消息莫过于Andrej Karpathy加入Anthropic。这位前OpenAI和特斯拉的AI研究专家在Twitter上宣布：
"个人动态：我已经加入Anthropic。我认为接下来几年在LLM前沿将特别具有形成性。我非常兴奋能够加入这里的团队并回到研发工作。我对教育仍然充满热情，计划在适当的时候恢复我在这方面的工作。"
这一举动引发了业界的广泛关注。正如Dan Shipper在推文中所问："Karpathy看到了什么？"而风投家Matt Turck则开玩笑地说道："重大新闻：Anthropic获得圣徒地位，正式受到AI耶稣的加冕。"

🚀 大模型竞赛白热化

Google今天发布的Gemini 3.5 Flash展现出令人印象深刻的性能提升。Box CEO Aaron Levie在详细测试报告中指出，新模型在复杂文档任务上比前代产品提升了12个百分点：
"在我们的测试中，Gemini 3.5 Flash在各个行业都有显著提升：金融服务从73%提升到81%（+8pp），公共部门从59%提升到76%（+17pp），医疗保健从51%提升到73%（+22pp），生命科学从47%提升到67%（+20pp）。"
Google还同时发布了多项创新产品。通过@joshwoodward的推文，我们了解到Gemini Spark——一个24/7个人AI代理已经推出，"专为主动管理任务和帮助您导航数字生活而设计"。

💰 计算资源成为新石油

令人瞩目的是，Sam Altman今天宣布了一项史无前例的举措——为Y Combinator当期所有初创公司各投资200万美元的Token：
"我很兴奋看到tokenmaxxing初创公司会发生什么，无论是它们内部的工作方式还是它们能够构建的产品。OpenAI提出向当前YC批次的每家初创公司投资200万美元的Token。愉快构建吧！"
这一举动凸显了一个重要趋势：计算资源正成为AI时代的稀缺商品。Altman还表示，"客户越来越要求我们提供容量确定性。随着模型变得更好，我们预计世界将在一段时间内受到容量限制。"Box CEO Aaron Levie也证实了这一观点，他刚从一场财富500强CIO晚餐回来，"Token成本将成为企业AI的主导话题"。

🛠️ AI代理基础设施成熟

Anthropic今天发布了两项重要的基础设施更新：自托管沙盒和MCP隧道。这些功能让企业能够在自己控制的环境中运行AI代理，同时保持与内部系统的安全连接。 与此同时，开发者工具也在快速演进。Ryan分享了他现在的工作流程——"我现在使用Composer 2.5进行规划、构建和迭代、调试。这是一个很棒的全能工具，特别适合UI工作。" Swyx也详细描述了他的四步AI软件开发生命周期，从测试到规划再到实施，展现了AI如何彻底改变软件开发流程。
从人才流动到技术突破，从资源分配到基础设施建设，AI行业正在经历一个关键的拐点。正如投资者Nikunj所观察到的："AI已经正式进入扩散时代（不是扩散模型），模型需要扩散到他们所做的一切。这将需要接下来的10-20年时间。"我们正处在一个从实验走向大规模应用的历史时刻。
